habitat: Pairs or family groups in montane mist-belt forest and in lowland and coastal evergreen forest.
summary: A common, localised endemic resident. At rest it has a matt-green body and a crested head with white markings. The upper tail and folded wings are iridescent greenish blue. The eye-rings and bill are red, and the wings are red in flight. Sexes are alike. Immatures are duller, with no further detail. The call is a slow kerk-kerk-kerk-kawk-kawk-kawk-kawk, with a high kek-kek-kek-kek alarm in flight, and a hoarse hurr hurr when people are near. No openly licensed research-grade photo was found in the Kruger box. No Kemp estimate is stored.

calls.description: A slow kerk-kerk-kerk-kawk-kawk-kawk-kawk. The alarm in flight is a high kek-kek-kek-kek. Near people it gives a hoarse hurr, hurr. Grade A call from near Kurland, Garden Route, Western Cape. The filename is XC1161576-260310-090406-Knysna-Turaco-A.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common, localised endemic resident, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Livingstone’s Turaco and Schalow’s Turaco are comparisons Newman names and are not in this list. No Kemp block was present, and the empty population estimate was left unchanged.
